q: How do I choose my first tattoo?
a: Start with placement and size, then narrow by style and subject. Pick a body area you are comfortable showing, decide roughly how many centimetres you want, and only then look for a design that fits that space. Save several references rather than settling on one.

Size follows placement. Fine detail needs room, so a design that reads well at 10 cm on a forearm can turn into a solid shape at 3 cm on a finger. The size guide shows 3, 5 and 10 cm on a real forearm so you can compare before you commit.

People report very different experiences, and comfort depends on the area, the session length and the individual. Outer arm and outer thigh are commonly described as easier than ribs, hands or feet. Ask your artist what to expect for the specific area you have in mind.

q: Can I bring reference images to an artist?
a: Yes, and most artists prefer it. Bring several references and be ready to say what you like about each one - the line weight, the level of detail, the way it follows the body. Ask how the design should be adapted to your anatomy instead of copying another tattoo exactly.

q: How do I save tattoo ideas?
a: Tap the bookmark on any image to add it to your collection. Saving works without an account and stays in your browser, and you can open the collection later or share the link with your artist.
